explain.say: Look at the shipwreck and what follows. Crusoe salvages tools, keeps a journal, cuts notches in a post as a calendar, tames goats, learns to bake bread and make pots, and lists it all. Why do all these small details make the story feel true?

explain.say: The critic Ian Watt, in 1957, called this formal realism. On the left, older romance: knights, marvels, far-off places. On the right, the new novel: one ordinary person, a real time and place, plain detailed prose. Which kind of story do you read most?

Look at the footprint: after fifteen years alone, one human print in the sand terrifies him. Later he rescues a man from cannibals, names him Friday after the day, and teaches him to call Crusoe Master. What does that first word tell you about their relationship?

faq.q: Why is Robinson Crusoe called the first English novel?
faq.a: It is one of the earliest long prose fictions about an ordinary individual in a realistic time and place, told in plain detail. Critics like Ian Watt saw it as a starting point of the novel, though earlier claims exist.
asks: Is Robinson Crusoe the first novel?

faq.a: Ian Watt's term for the novel's way of imitating real life: particular people, specific times and places, and detailed, ordinary language.
A man Crusoe rescues from cannibals and names after the day of the week. He becomes Crusoe's servant and convert, and is taught to call him Master.

faq.q: Was Robinson Crusoe based on a real person?
faq.a: Partly. The Scottish sailor Alexander Selkirk was marooned on an island off Chile from 1704 to 1709, and his story was well known. Defoe changed the setting and much more.

faq.q: How do postcolonial critics read Robinson Crusoe?
faq.a: They see Crusoe's claiming of the island, his renaming and mastery of Friday, and his slave-trading voyage as a model of colonial thinking. J. M. Coetzee's novel Foe rewrites the story.

Ian Watt's The Rise of the Novel was published in 1957.
